newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude skids, heat reverses on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude skids, heat reverses on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures sold off sharply in mid-afternoon trading Friday as traders took profits ahead of the weekend.

January crude oil closed at $23.71 a barrel, slumping from a high of $24.31 during the session and down 13 cents on the day. December heating oil sold off sharply from a high of 74.90 cents a gallon to end at 72.60 cents as it was sold in favor of gasoline as traders took profits.
"The market is down because it has been in a selling mode and the spreads were never working," said Ralph D'Esposito, a trader at RJ Futures.

Traders also said that market participants were less worried about forecasts of colder weather over the next week to 10 days and were starting to pay more attention to reports this week that diplomats saw some momentum picking up toward implementing the Iraq-United Nations oil-for-food deal.
"It was enough on very light volume to get some people unwinding" their positions, said Nauman Barakat, a trader at Prudential Securities.

December gasoline ended up 76 points at 67.80 cents a gallon. Heating oil had been rising versus gasoline over the past three weeks and was at a 6.81 cents premium at the close on Thursday. That eroded to 4.80 by the end of Friday.
"The market didn't like it enough to take it into the weekend and then we saw some commission-house selling," said D'Esposito.
The holiday period at the end of next week when the market will be closed from Thursday through the weekend, coinciding as it does with an OPEC meeting, also was keeping players wary.
